findings.description: The delivery guard reads only delivery.registry_receipt, delivery.tag_receipt and delivery.ci_receipt; nothing requires a phase-20 registry_publication entry. tools/test_ci.py:311-330 selects publications[-1], which is still the phase-17 0.2.1 record, so with workspace version 0.2.2 the function returns at line 330 and every receipt-specific assertion is skipped, including the CHANGELOG receipt-link check at line 349. A full delivery can therefore satisfy release_delivery.verify while the 0.2.2 receipt links in README.md:40-42, CHANGELOG.md:6-8, docs/RELEASE.md:5-7 and docs/STABILITY.md are never validated against an actual receipt. Unlike attempt 01, this is no longer misdescribed: docs/phase-status.json:4559-4567 now records planned_registry_publication with the exact required transition, a mandatory tools/test_ci.py execution after registry verification, and an explicit enforcement_boundary stating that release_delivery.py does not enforce this metadata. The gap is therefore an accurately disclosed manual obligation rather than a false claim, but it is still unenforced at the point where it matters.
findings.required_fix: At delivery, create phases[20].registry_publication with status published_and_verified, version "0.2.2", evidence "docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.2.json" and the actual source_commit, then run tools/test_ci.py and retain its output before the delivery commit; docs/phase-status.json is fingerprint-excluded (tools/review_phase.py:15-16) so this needs no re-qualification. In the next qualified source change, add an assertion in tools/release_delivery.py near line 136 that phases[20].registry_publication.version == VERSION and its evidence equals the canonical registry receipt path, so the current-version document guard cannot be silently skipped.

findings.description: verify_release_readiness carries the docstring "Publication helpers must require this accepted, current-source assessment", but no publication helper calls it. Grepping the repository shows its only callers are tools/test_release_delivery.py:195 and :205; scripts/verify-publication.py imports only scripts/check-package.py (line 17) and never consults a review record, and tools/release_delivery.py does not reference it either. The accepted plan requires an actual Claude review before publishing (docs/g25-response-compatibility-plan.md:123-124), yet 0.2.2 could be published and its registry receipt recorded with no accepted readiness review at the current source, and nothing would detect it. Read charitably the docstring is an obligation on future helpers rather than a claim of present behaviour, and phase completion is separately machine-gated (review_phase.py:385-386 plus release_delivery.verify), so the impact is bounded to the publication step itself.
findings.required_fix: Either wire the control in — have scripts/verify-publication.py (or a thin pre-publication helper) require review_phase.verify_release_readiness to succeed for the current fingerprint before writing docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.2.json, with a negative test in tools/test_release_delivery.py — or reword the docstring to state plainly that the readiness review is a procedural maintainer gate that no tool enforces, and record that boundary alongside the existing enforcement_boundary note in the phase-20 record.

findings.description: For 0.2.2 the published-archive verification requires only that examples/response_defaults.rs was executed from the archive; it has no equivalent requirement for the new examples/response_compatibility.rs, which is the consumer that actually demonstrates this patch's fix. The four-example and three-consumer requirement lives only in scripts/check-access-release.py:38-51, which runs in the candidate gate and requires releaseCommit == HEAD, so it cannot be rerun after a receipt-bearing delivery commit (docs/phase-status.json:4530). At delivery time tools/release_delivery.py:147-148 calls publication.require_proof, which checks only the six generic command prefixes, so the G25 consumer execution is not re-asserted against the published artifact. The evidence still exists in the immutable gate record and the published file rows are byte-compared to the qualified proof, so this is a guard-coverage gap rather than missing evidence.
findings.required_fix: Extend the conditional at scripts/verify-publication.py:78-82 to require the response_compatibility example run whenever examples/response_compatibility.rs is present in the published archive (mirroring scripts/check-access-release.py:38-44), and add the corresponding negative case to tools/test_release_022.py. This changes packaged tooling only outside crates/scm-sdk, but schedule it with the next qualified source change if it would disturb the current archives.

findings.description: The delivery procedure requires "actual terminal success for all 49 configured CI jobs before phase completion" and tools/release_delivery.py:94-96 additionally requires refs/heads/main to equal the CI run commit, yet no document in the repository mentions [skip ci] — while every recent commit (d64d9dc, 938adbe, e4cabb0, 2908a98, 16e4cf7) carries it. The chunk attempt-02 reviewer asked for this in docs/RELEASE.md and docs/CI.md; the maintainer instead recorded it only in docs/phase-status.json:4528 delivery_execution_constraints, which is fingerprint-excluded bookkeeping rather than the procedure a maintainer follows. A delivery push that keeps the habitual marker would produce no run for the final main commit and block the next chunk's required receipt.
findings.required_fix: State in docs/RELEASE.md's delivery steps (and mirror in docs/CI.md's delivery section) that the commit pushed to main for delivery must not contain [skip ci] or any other skip marker, because the terminal 49-job receipt must belong to that exact commit, and that only post-review receipt-only bookkeeping commits may skip CI.

findings.description: docs/SECURITY.md is declared phase and chunk scope evidence, but its Runtime boundaries section still describes only request-side enforcement and the rule that returned URLs remain data; it never discloses that response modes no longer assert the uuid, rfc3339, datetime, date, duration, email, url and regex string formats across the 172 frozen roots reached by the shared relaxation. The disclosure is complete in CHANGELOG.md:13-15, docs/VALIDATION.md:114-119 and docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:13, and the maintainer dispositioned this as accepted_documentation_location (docs/phase-status.json:4454-4458) without claiming any guarantee for ignored formats, so this is an omission in the one document a security reader would consult first rather than an inaccuracy.
findings.required_fix: Add one bullet to the Runtime boundaries list noting that response validation deliberately ignores the eight named string-format assertions while retaining string types, baseline presence/type/bounds, finite JSON and resource limits, with a link to docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md for the full loosened/retained rule set. Batch it with the next qualified source change, since it alters packaged-adjacent documentation in the source fingerprint.

findings.description: The PROTECTED tuple is dead: verify() never references it (unlike scripts/check-release-candidate.py:25-29, from which this file was derived), so a reader is led to expect a protected-path comparison that does not happen. Relatedly, RELEASES[(20, '0.2.2')] = '80baf80f0f6d90f9b382e8895083ca30fa5e8997' is only echoed into docs/checks/phase-20-candidate.json:5 as baselineCommit; nothing diffs the release against it, so that recorded value carries no verified meaning. The actual guarantees of this checker (HEAD binding, archive re-hash, inventory, VCS and full byte comparison) are strong and unaffected.
findings.required_fix: Remove the unused PROTECTED constant, and either drop baselineCommit from the receipt or make it meaningful by asserting that no path outside the declared release scope changed since that commit. Carry this with the next qualified source change so the current archives stay valid.

findings.description: Three prose integers in the document that describes CI remain untested: "The complete local Phase 20 gate has 59 commands" (line 150), "CI's 41-command subset" (line 158) and the hardcoded credential-free count at line 106. I confirmed all three are currently correct (59 from commands_for(20); 41 after ci_commands_for removes the 14 check-rust, 2 check-native-exports, 1 check-access-release and generate_models --verify-fixtures entries), but tools/test_ci.py binds only the job counts and the scripts inventory, not these numerals, so a future change to commands_for(20) would leave them silently wrong. findings.required_fix: Add an assertion in tools/test_ci.py parsing the integers from the "complete local Phase 20 gate has N commands", "N-command subset" and "N credential-free commands" phrases and comparing them to len(commands_for(20)) and len(ci_commands_for(20)). This changes the source fingerprint, so batch it with the next qualified source change rather than invalidating the d64d9dc archives.

findings.description: Typed-over-raw precedence is implemented correctly and emits no duplicate keys, but for the request-reachable projection models (TargetMetadata, LanguageOption and the three JobCreateRequestJobMetadataVariant models) a set typed projection causes the same-key extension entry to be skipped during serialization, so a caller who populates both silently loses the raw value from the request body. This is documented only in markdown (CHANGELOG.md:21-28, docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:17); the generated projection fields and Extensions carry no rustdoc, so a consumer reading docs.rs for published 0.2.2 cannot discover it. The maintainer has restated this as final_markdown_only_for_this_release (docs/phase-status.json:4508-4512) and claims no rustdoc delivery, so it is a recorded deferral.
findings.required_fix: In a future patch with its own archive proofs, emit a short generated doc comment on the vendor-added projection fields and on Extensions stating that a set typed projection supersedes a same-key extension on serialization and that callers must leave the projection unset to serialize a preserved raw value.

Because release_delivery.verify requires the current fingerprint to equal the reviewed source and both published and CI commits to fingerprint to it, any source change made to address my low findings invalidates the d64d9dc archives and forces re-packaging and re-qualification. Their evidence enters the gate indirectly through check-access-release.py's re-extraction, inventory, VCS and full byte comparison, which I judged sound, but I could not observe the package runs inside the gate record.
